question: Using Figure 2A-1 and Section 2A.11, describe the requirements for a retroreflective strip used on a sign support to enhance conspicuity.
model_answer: Direct Answer: A retroreflective strip on a sign support is a permitted method of enhancing sign conspicuity, but once used it must meet mandatory dimensional and color requirements. The strip must be at least 2 inches wide, run the full length of the support from the sign to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, and match the sign's background color (red for YIELD and DO NOT ENTER signs), with no legend or other information displayed on it. A parallel requirement applies to Crossbuck supports at passive grade crossings, where a white strip of the same dimensions is mandatory on the back of the support. Standards (mandatory): - "If a strip of retroreflective material is used on the sign support, it shall be at least 2 inches in width, it shall be placed for the full length of the support from the sign to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, and its color shall match the background color of the sign, except that the color of the strip for the YIELD and DO NOT ENTER signs shall be red. The retroreflective strip shall not display any legend or other information." - For grade crossings: "A vertical strip of retroreflective white material, not less than 2 inches in width, shall be used on each Crossbuck support at passive grade crossings for the full length of the back of the support from the Crossbuck sign or Number of Tracks plaque to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway," with a wrapped strip on a round support of at least 2 inches outside diameter satisfying the requirement. Options (permitted): - Based upon engineering judgment, where improvement of the conspicuity of a standard regulatory, warning, or guide sign is desired, adding a strip of retroreflective material to the sign support is one of the methods that may be used (see Figure 2A-1). Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2A-1, item E, illustrates a vertical retroreflective strip on a sign support (matching the fluorescent yellow-green background of the pedestrian warning sign) extending down the support and ending "2 ft MAX." above the near edge of the roadway. - [Image 2] shows the same Figure 2A-1 in its page context (Page 48), including item E with the 2-foot maximum dimension above the roadway edge. - [Image 4] shows Section 2A.11 Standard Paragraph 5 stating the 2-inch minimum width, full-length placement, background-matching color (red for YIELD and DO NOT ENTER), and prohibition on any legend, along with the list of permitted conspicuity methods including item L (retroreflective strip on the sign support). - [Image 3] shows Section 2A.21/2A.22, whose Support text notes that information on retroreflective material on sign supports is contained in Section 2A.11. - [Image 5] shows Figure 8B-2, depicting the 2-inch white retroreflective strip on the back of the Crossbuck support (and an optional 2-inch red or white strip on the front) terminating within 2 feet of the roadway edge. Citations: - Section 2A.11 Standard §5 (p.49) - Section 2A.11 Option §1 (p.49) - Section 8B.04 Standard §17 (p.1000) - Section 2A.21 Support §8 (p.62) - Figure 2A-1 (p.48)
gold_answer: The strip must be at least 2 inches wide, extend from the sign down the full support to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, match the sign background color except that YIELD and DO NOT ENTER strips are red, and contain no legend or other information.
